claim.claim-text: 1. A peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) for use in the therapeutic or prophylactic treatment of a bacterial infection, preferably a bacterial infection that results in diarrhea or a bacterial urogenital, preferably vaginal infection, wherein the PGH is a polypeptide selected from the group consisting of:

2. A peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) for use in the therapeutic or prophylactic treatment of a bacterial infection, preferably a bacterial infection that results in diarrhea or a bacterial urogenital, preferably vaginal infection, wherein the PGH is encoded by a nucleic acid comprising or consisting of a nucleic acid sequence selected from the group consisting of:

3. A recombinant vector comprising a nucleic acid according to claim 2 for producing a PGH for use according to claim 2, preferably a viral or episomal vector, preferably a baculovirus vector, lentivirus vector, adenovirus vector, vaccinia or retroviral vector, yeast or bacterial episomal vector.

4. A host cell producing and/or secreting a PGH for use according to claim 1 or a PGH for use according to claim 2, comprising a nucleic acid as defined in claim 2 or a vector according to claim 3, preferably a host cell selected from the group consisting of yeast cells, preferably Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Pichia pastoris cells, bacterial E. coli, Vibrio notriegens or B. subtilis cells, plant cells, preferably Nicotiana tabacum or Physcomirella patens cells, NIH-3T3, HEK293, HEK293T, CHO and COS mammalian cells, and insect cells, preferably sf9 insect cells

5. Pharmaceutical composition comprising a PGH as defined in claim 1, a PGH encoded by the nucleic acids as defined in claim 2, a recombinant vector as defined in claim 3 or a host cell as defined in claim 4 and at least one physiologically acceptable excipient.
6. A peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH)-secreting probiotic bacterial strain selected from the group consisting of

Lactococcus lactis, preferably subsp. lactis and subsp. cremoris, Lactobacillus gasseri, Lactobacillus crispatus, Lactobacillus jensenii, Lactobacillus plantarum CCOS 893 (DSM 32352), Lactobacillus fermentum, Lactobacillus johnsonii, Lactobacillus rhamnosus, Lactobacillus paracasei, Lactobacillus casei, Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis, Bifidobacterium longum, Bifidobacterium breve, Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum and Bifidobacterium bifidum,
for use in the therapeutic or prophylactic treatment of a bacterial infection, optionally a bacterial infection that results in diarrhea or is a bacterial urogenital, preferably vaginal infection.

7. The peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH)-secreting probiotic bacterial strain for use according to claim 6, wherein the bacterial infection is caused by a pathogenic microorganism selected from the group consisting of enteroinvasive Escherichia coli, enterohaemorragic Escherichia coli, diarrheagenic Escherichia coli, Helicobacter pylori, Salmonella enterica, Shigella flexneri and sonnei, Campylobacter jejuni, Listeria monocytogenes, Bacillus cereus, Vibrio cholerae, Staphylococcus aureus, Gardnerella vaginalis, Clostridium perfringens and Clostridium difficile, preferably the pathogenic microorganism is Clostridium difficile.

8. The peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH)-secreting probiotic bacterial strain for use according to any of claims 6 or 7, wherein the peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) is selected from the group consisting of:

9. The peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH)-secreting probiotic bacterial strain for use according to any of claims 6 to 8, wherein the probiotic bacterial strain is selected from the group consisting of Lactococcus lactis CCOS 949 (DSM 32294), Lactobacillus gasseri CCOS 960 (DSM 32296); Lactobacillus crispatus CCOS 961 (CCOS 961); Lactobacillus plantarum CCOS 893 (DSM 32352); Lactobacillus johnsonii CCOS 824 (CCOS 824); Lactobacillus paracasei subsp. paracasei CCOS 1205 (CCOS 1205); Lactobacillus paracasei subsp. paracasei CCOS 1201 (CCOS 1201); Lactobacillus fermentum CCOS 1030 (CCOS 1030); Lactobacillus jensenii CCOS 962 (CCOS 962); Lactobacillus rhamnosus CCOS 965 (CCOS 965); Bifidobacterium bifidum CCOS 571 (CCOS 571); Bifidobacterium longum CCOS 974 (CCOS 974); Bifidobacterium breve CCOS 971 (CCOS 971) and Bifidobacterium breve CCOS 586 (CCOS 586), preferably, the probiotic bacterial strain is Lactococcus lactis CCOS 949 (DSM 32294).

10. A composition comprising the probiotic bacterial strain, preferably Lactococcus lactis, more preferably subspecies lactis or subspecies cremoris, for use according to any of claims 6 to 9, further comprising

11. The composition for use according to claim 10, wherein the N-acetylated monosaccharide is selected from the group consisting of N-acetylglucosamine, N-acetylgalactosamine, N-acetyl-hexosamine, N-acetylmannosamine, and mixtures thereof.

12. The composition for use according to any of claims 10 or 11, wherein the prebiotic carbon source is selected from the group consisting of a fructooligosaccharide, galactooligosac-charide, glyco-oligosaccharide, lactulose, xylooligosaccharide, isomaltooligosaccharide, and mixtures thereof.

13. The composition for use according to any one of claims 10 to 12, wherein the at least one sulfur source is selected from the group consisting of methionine, cysteine, cystine, cysta-thionine, a sulfur-containing inorganic salt, preferably magnesium sulfate, sodium or potassium thiosulfate, and mixtures thereof.

14. The composition for use according to any one of claims 10 to 13, wherein the at least one nitrogen source is selected from the group consisting of ammonium salts, preferably ammonium chloride or citrate, urea, amino acids, preferably nitrogen-rich amino acids, more preferably glutamic acid, arginine, aspartic acid and/or alanine, as well as mixtures thereof.

15. Pharmaceutical composition comprising a peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH)-secreting probiotic bacterial strain as defined in any of claims 6 to 9, or a composition as defined in any of claims 10 to 14, and at least one physiologically acceptable excipient.
